title: EPAN: change over to using tvb_get_bits32 throughout the code base
description:
While at it, replace any 'old-style' encoding parameter, or ENC_NA
with the appropriate ENC_[LITTLE|BIG]_ENDIAN encoding flag.

notes.body: Will tvb_get_bits() be deprecated/removed?  I notice it is not in README.dissector
That is [my proposal](https://lists.wireshark.org/archives/wireshark-dev/202502/msg00014.html) (on wireshark-dev) yes.

I am in favour of this change and dropping tvb_get_bits() to encourage use of the most appropriate sized call instead.  Note that within this change, the changes to packet-oran.c are readying (at-most) 16-bit values into 32 bit fields.  To be honest I didn't know the other variants existed, and would prefer to be reading these values into a uint16_t.  Will fix for my next commit to that dissector.

The only thing I liked about the generic version was that it was obvious that you were reading a chosen number of bits, whereas the sized version might imply you were reading exactly 8/16/32/64 bits.
I don't see why we need all the variants surly reading to a wider variable poses no problem?

I would still prefer to get values of the appropriate size, so that I don't need to use a too-wide field or need to do an ugly cast to use the value.  I doubt there is any measurable performance difference (either way).

This is similar to proto_tree_add_item_ret_uint, where I reluctantly use uint32 but would often prefer the natural type.

In a next iteration I would like to add DISSECTOR_ASSERTs to the 8/16/32/64 bits version to make sure that not more than the returning type bitesize number of bits are requested. This would catch any inadvertent overflows.
check_typed_item_calls.py can be taught to catch obvious cases...

Still not getting wat the problem is. Seems silly to clutter the API with
unnecessary functions.

Den lör 22 feb. 2025 19:35Martin Mathieson (@martin.r.mathieson) <
gitlab@mg.gitlab.com> skrev:

The other functions were already there.

One downside of returning smaller integer types is that it may make numerical overflows more likely when calculations are done with these values.

Underlying problem is there are now multiple ways of getting at a similar (not same) result.  
Some history on these functions may help.  
With commit 43bb2aea51286c1b9c2d07e87f9a70374a849323 (28-04-2007) the function tvb_get_bits was introduced.  
With commit b688f9154aacf9c2f30dc6c715bc115a05e9fcef (18-05-2007) the function tvb_get_bits was split into tvb_get_bits[8|16|32|64]. These functions were tailored to their size, i.e., they returned that sized unsigned integer and they even checked if the requested no_of_bits was in range of the requested size. Not only too many, but also too few!  
With commit 9b36fc784e8edf1c018157bb43d64f5a24216c73 (14-11-2009) the function tvb_get_bits was reintroduced.  
With commit 075bd9f86a614f718e01dfb8952344e1ec6c710c (28-02-2012) all the restrictions were dropped, and tvb_get_bits made an alias for tvb_get_bits32.  
With commit 7b82110092a105eedd5209e4ed75416098161d1f (26-09-2021) little endian support introduced.  

With the removal of the 'too many or too few bits requested' restriction _any_ of these functions could be used to request any number of bits, regardless of the return size. So in effect tvb_get_bits became equivalent to tvb_get_bits32. The numeric extension on the name now only gives an indication of the size of the returned unsigned integer, that is, the number of bits you may request.  
I think that a check for that number of bits requested should be here, but that's another matter.  

In effect, the function tvb_get_bits has become obsolete (since 2012), in that it does not reflect the actual size of the value it can operate on, and, like Martin said, a suitable set of explicit functions is already there.
Right, got it now.
Can the `(int)` casts in `packet-gsm_a_rr.c` be dropped?
Apparently they can :grinning:

@@ -71,7 +71,7 @@ dissect_peap(tvbuff_t *tvb, packet_info *pinfo, proto_tree *tree, void *data _U_
   }
 
   if (!(   len >= 5
-        && tvb_get_bits(tvb, offset, 16, ENC_BIG_ENDIAN) == tvb_get_bits(eap_tvb, 0, 16, ENC_BIG_ENDIAN)
+        && tvb_get_bits32(tvb, offset, 16, ENC_BIG_ENDIAN) == tvb_get_bits32(eap_tvb, 0, 16, ENC_BIG_ENDIAN)
         && tvb_get_uint16(tvb, offset + 2, ENC_BIG_ENDIAN) <= tvb_get_uint16(eap_tvb, 2, ENC_BIG_ENDIAN)
         && (
                 (tvb_get_uint8(eap_tvb, 0) == EAP_REQUEST && tvb_get_uint8(tvb, offset + 4) == EAP_TYPE_ID)

@@ -13482,10 +13482,10 @@ proto_tree_add_split_bits_crumb(proto_tree *tree, const int hfindex, tvbuff_t *t
 	proto_tree_add_text_internal(tree, tvb, start, length,

-						 tvb_get_bits(tvb,

-							      crumb_spec[crumb_index].crumb_bit_length,
-							      ENC_BIG_ENDIAN),

+							        bit_offset,
+							        crumb_spec[crumb_index].crumb_bit_length,
+							        ENC_BIG_ENDIAN),
